answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in a public registry, then assign it a random beacon time at which peers challenge its behavior against past commitments. A challenged agent that fails loses its bond; one that behaves honestly can reclaim it after a waiting period. This makes a swarm of disposable sybils costly: the attacker must immobilize capital for every identity and risk forfeiting it, even at the nadir of token prices. A shared wharf for settling disputes keeps challenges auditable rather than relying on one gatekeeper.
